title: There is, there isn't
goal: Say that something exists or doesn't, ask yes/no questions with *mı*, and count from zero to a million.
bekal: use *var* and *yok* for existence and possession
make yes/no questions with *mı/mi/mu/mü*, written as a separate word

notes: **Var and yok are a pair, and neither is a verb.** *Var* means "there is, available", *yok* means "there isn't". Note that you don't negate *var* with *değil* — Turkish has a separate word for that.

**There is no verb "to have" in Turkish.** Instead you say "my X exists": *arkadaşım var* = "my friend exists" = I have a friend. *Param yok* = "my money doesn't exist" = I have no money. The thing gets a possessive ending first, then *var* or *yok* closes the sentence.

**Değil mi? is a tag question** — "isn't it?", "aren't you?", "right?". It goes at the end of the sentence to ask for agreement, and its form never changes, no matter who the sentence is about: *Güzel, değil mi?*, *Öğrencisin, değil mi?*

**Amca, teyze, abi, abla are used with strangers.** Literally "uncle, aunt, big brother, big sister", but Turks use them for anyone a little or a lot older. Calling the shopkeeper *amca* is far warmer than calling him *bey*.

sections.title: Asking with mı — a word that stands alone

blocks.text: To make a yes/no question, Turkish doesn't swap the word order or add a helper like *do*. It adds one particle: **mı / mi / mu / mü**, chosen by vowel harmony and **written separately** from the word before it.

Look at the last two rows: the person ending **moves onto the particle**. Not *öğrencisin mi*, but *öğrenci misin*. The rule holds: the question particle stands alone as a word, and the person ending attaches to it.

blocks.title: Where it goes decides what it means
items: *mı* is placed after **the word being asked about**, and moving it changes the meaning of the sentence:

*Budi yarın Ankara'ya mı gidiyor?* — "Is it to ANKARA that Budi is going tomorrow?" · *Budi yarın mı Ankara'ya gidiyor?* — "Is it TOMORROW that Budi is going to Ankara?" · *Budi mi yarın Ankara'ya gidiyor?* — "Is it BUDI who is going to Ankara tomorrow?"
If nothing needs highlighting, put it at the end of the sentence, before the person ending — that's the neutral form.

blocks.text: If your question uses a question word — *ne*, *kim*, *nerede*, *kaç* — the particle *mı* is NOT used. *Bu ne mi?* is wrong; the right form is *Bu ne?*

Compound numbers are said **from largest to smallest, with no linking word at all**: *on bir* (11), *yirmi beş* (25), *kırk yedi* (47), *yüz elli* (150), *bin dokuz yüz doksan dokuz* (1999). No "and", no hyphen — just line them up.

blocks.title: Bin without bir, yüz without bir
items: "A hundred" is *yüz*, not *bir yüz*. "A thousand" is *bin*, not *bir bin*. Adding *bir* in front of either sounds like a foreigner's mistake — and it usually is.
But from a million up, *bir* is required again: *bir milyon*, *bir milyar*.
